clue.text: Retail worker overwhelmed by thank-you letters' positive conclusions

indicators.note: to be overwhelmed by something is to be engulfed by it, so the worker sits inside the thank-you

parts.note: French for thank you, as familiar in English
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

indicators.note: conclusions are endings, so only the closing letter of each of the two words is kept

parts.note: final letter of the word
final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A shop assistant is buried under thank-you letters that all end on an upbeat note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retail worker' reads as one phrase, but 'Retail' alone is the definition, used as a verb. MERC(HAND)I + SE gives MERCHANDISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To merchandise goods is to promote and sell them in shops, which is what retailing them means as a verb.

clue.text: Almost dead bone found in burial place possibly

indicators.note: something found in a place lies inside it, so the bone goes within the burial place

parts.note: a burial mound or barrow; 'possibly' flags an example
a rib is a bone of the chest

explanation.surface: An archaeologist finds a bone in what might be a grave, belonging to someone nearly dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost dead bone' tempts a solver to read 'dead bone' together; the definition stops at 'dead'.
explanation.definitionFit: Moribund describes someone or something at the point of death or in terminal decline.

clue.text: Silly person finally gives incomprehensible answer

indicators.note: silly says the letters are jumbled in a foolish way

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of each of the two words gives and incomprehensible

explanation.surface: A foolish person ends up giving an answer nobody can follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incomprehensible' looks like the anagram signal, but it only gives its last letter; 'Silly' is what jumbles 'person'.
explanation.definitionFit: A response is a reply given to a question, so it is a synonym of answer.

clue.text: Prostitute has no right to become a physicist

indicators.note: to have no right means the letter standing for right must be dropped

parts.note: slang for a prostitute
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A sex worker without any rights hopes to become a scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: HOOKER loses its R. Robert Hooke was the 17th-century English scientist behind Hooke's law of elasticity.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Hooke studied elasticity and light and gave his name to a law of springs, making him a famous physicist.

clue.text: Number 10 in a certain context worried for new arrival

parts.note: in the periodic table, element number 10 is neon
as in 'what's eating you?', to eat someone is to worry them

explanation.surface: Someone at Number 10 Downing Street is anxious about a newcomer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number 10' suggests Downing Street; the 'certain context' is chemistry, where atomic number 10 is neon.
explanation.definitionFit: A neonate is a newborn baby, literally someone who has just arrived in the world.

clue.text: Get Back central to popular US TV series, not just any number

indicators.note: being central to two things puts it in the middle, between them

parts.note: fashionable, in vogue
ER is the American hospital drama

indicators.note: going back means the word before it is read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Get Back, the Beatles documentary, sits at the heart of a well-loved American television show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get Back' looks like the Beatles song or film, but 'Back' is the turnaround signal. ER is the long-running American hospital drama.
explanation.definitionFit: An integer is a whole number, a particular kind of number rather than any fraction or decimal.

clue.text: Former Tory securing millions in a mostly big exchange of land

parts.note: an ex is a former partner, so the prefix means former

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast inside, so the Tory word wraps what follows
the millions letter is placed inside the next pieces

parts.note: Con is the abbreviation for Conservative
taken as written
M is the abbreviation for million

indicators.note: mostly means not all of the word, so its last letter is lost

parts.note: taken as written, before trimming

explanation.surface: A one-time Conservative pockets millions from a huge property swap.
explanation.walkthrough: The millions letter goes inside 'a' plus the trimmed 'big', and the Tory abbreviation wraps that. Excambion is a term from Scots law.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots law an excambion is a contract by which one piece of land is swapped for another.

clue.text: Some enthusiastic church reformer

indicators.note: some of a word means only part of it, so the answer lies inside the next word

parts.note: letters three to five of the word

explanation.surface: A zealous churchman pushes for reform.
explanation.walkthrough: Jan Hus was a Czech priest burnt at the stake in 1415, a forerunner of the Protestant Reformation.
explanation.definitionFit: Jan Hus campaigned to reform the Catholic Church a century before Luther, so he is a classic church reformer.

clue.text: Musical act shows style

parts.note: Hair is the 1960s rock musical
to act is to do

explanation.surface: A song-and-dance number shows off a certain flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Musical' looks like an adjective describing the act; it is the noun, the show Hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairdo is the style in which someone's hair is cut and arranged.

clue.text: Head of state made a political broadcast in favour of the introduction of Musk's X perhaps

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only the start of the next word is kept

parts.note: first letter of the word

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered widely, so the preceding words are strewn into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
to be for something is to favour it

indicators.note: an introduction comes first, so only the opening letter of the next word counts

parts.note: first letter of the name

explanation.surface: A head of state gives a party political broadcast backing the arrival of Elon Musk's X.
explanation.walkthrough: S + scrambled MADE A POLITICAL + FOR + M gives SOCIAL MEDIA PLATFORM; 'broadcast' looks part of 'political broadcast' but is the shuffle signal.
explanation.definitionFit: X, formerly Twitter and owned by Elon Musk, is one example of an online network where users post and share content.

clue.text: See 27
Part of eye movement that can't be controlled after operation date is cancelled initially

indicators.note: after places the twitch after the operation

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary twitch

indicators.note: initially means take just the first letter of cancelled

explanation.surface: An eye twitch after surgery, once the appointment is called off.
explanation.definitionFit: The optic disc is the spot on the retina where the optic nerve leaves the eye.

clue.text: One expected to make a comeback — was a manager in, say, a period of growth earlier

definitions.text: One expected to make a comeback

indicators.note: placed earlier means this piece goes in front of the rest

parts.note: an economic boom

indicators.note: the managing word sits inside the abbreviation for say

parts.note: e.g., for example, is what 'say' means in 'a fruit, say'
to run a business is to manage it

explanation.surface: A former boss is tipped to return, having run things in a boom time.
explanation.walkthrough: BOOM + E(RAN)G. 'One expected to make a comeback' sounds like a sports star or a politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A boomerang is a curved throwing stick that is designed to fly back to the thrower.

clue.text: See 8
Former tennis player mostly very unpleasant like Edberg initially

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: nasty means very unpleasant
as means like, in the same way

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the name before it

parts.note: first letter of the name

explanation.surface: A one-time tennis star was mostly rather horrid, just like Stefan Edberg.
explanation.walkthrough: Ilie Nastase was a Romanian world number one in the 1970s, known for his temper; Edberg is another tennis star, here just a source of E.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilie Nastase won the US Open and French Open and was the first official ATP number one, a retired tennis champion.

clue.text: Welcome inspiring fellows following a concert

indicators.note: following means coming after, so this assembly is placed after the article

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the welcome takes the fellows inside it

parts.note: to greet is to welcome
fellows are men

explanation.surface: Fans give an uplifting reception to some chaps after a gig.
explanation.walkthrough: A + GREE(MEN)T. 'Concert' looks like a musical event, but it means harmony, as in acting 'in concert'.
explanation.definitionFit: Concert in the sense of acting in concert means accord or harmony of purpose, which is agreement.

clue.text: Heartless confrontation causes havoc

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle letter of the next word is removed

parts.note: a run-in is a quarrel or clash

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted clash wreaks destruction.
explanation.walkthrough: RUN-IN loses its central N. 'Causes havoc' reads as a verb phrase, but 'causes' only links; 'havoc' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruin as a noun means wholesale destruction and devastation, which is what havoc is.

clue.text: Energy provider at last involved in rising fuels for Turkish palace

indicators.note: involved in means put inside, so these letters go into the reversed fuels
rising in a down clue means the letters read upwards, so the fuels word is turned round

parts.note: oil and gas are both fuels
E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of provider

explanation.surface: An energy supplier ends up caught up in rising fuel prices.
explanation.walkthrough: OIL and GAS, read upwards in the down clue, give SAGLIO; E and R (the end of provider) go inside after S.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraglio was the harem quarters, or the whole palace, of the Ottoman sultan in Turkey.

clue.text: See 8
Dangerous beast demolished half of plates, dishes etc.

indicators.note: demolishing half of something knocks down half, so only half of the word survives

parts.note: crockery is the general word for plates, dishes and cups

explanation.surface: A wild animal on the rampage has smashed half the tableware.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half of CROCKERY survives; a croc is informal for a crocodile.
explanation.definitionFit: A croc is short for crocodile, a large reptile that can kill people.

clue.text: Traditional Russian or Ukrainian function with dry white wine

parts.note: cos is the short form of the cosine function in trigonometry
sack is an old name for dry white wines such as sherry

explanation.surface: A traditional Slavic celebration where dry white wine is served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Function' looks like a party; it is the mathematical cosine. Sack is the Shakespearean name for sherry, beloved of Falstaff.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cossacks were the free warrior communities of the Russian and Ukrainian steppes, now a traditional identity.

clue.text: Keep secret visit short, previously being drunk

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about unsteadily, so these letters lurch into a new order
cut short means the final letter of the word is lost

parts.note: to call on someone is to visit them
once means at a former time

explanation.surface: Keep quiet about a brief drop-in made some time ago while tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: CAL and ONCE are shuffled together: 'being drunk' covers both pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To conceal something is to hide it from others, which is keeping it secret.

clue.text: Two characters promoted in TV detective's unit

indicators.note: promoting two characters moves a pair of letters higher up this down entry while the rest keep their places

parts.note: Columbo is the scruffy LA detective of the US TV series

explanation.surface: A couple of actors get a step up in the television detective's squad.
explanation.walkthrough: In COLUMBO, the U moves up above the L and the final O moves up above the M: COULOMB. 'Characters' here means letters, not cast members.
explanation.definitionFit: The coulomb is the SI unit of electric charge, named after the French physicist Charles-Augustin de Coulomb.

clue.text: Emphatically not wearing a suit

indicators.note: not wearing means not being in, so the little word for in is taken off

parts.note: 'in spades' means emphatically, to a great degree

explanation.surface: Someone loudly declares they are certainly not putting on a suit.
explanation.walkthrough: IN SPADES drops IN, since 'not wearing' means not in. 'Suit' looks like clothing but is a suit of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Spades is one of the four suits in a pack of playing cards, alongside hearts, diamonds and clubs.

clue.text: Break down clues at first, that will get you extremely far

definitions.text: that will get you extremely far

parts.note: to parse a sentence is to break it down into its grammatical parts

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Advice to solvers: analyse the clues first and you will go a long way.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as crossword advice; the definition is a light-hearted description of a vast astronomical distance.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsec is about 3.26 light years, so travelling one would take you an enormous distance.

clue.text: Canada's leader and others taking part in summits to find a way to end war

indicators.note: those taking part in something are inside it, so the leader and others go within the summits

parts.note: peaks are mountain summits

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the first letter of the country name is kept

parts.note: first letter of the country
et al. is Latin shorthand for 'and others'

explanation.surface: Canada's prime minister and fellow leaders attend summit meetings seeking an end to fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canada's leader' suggests the prime minister, but it only supplies a single letter. Et al. is Latin for 'and others'.
explanation.definitionFit: Peace talks are negotiations between warring sides aimed at agreeing a ceasefire and settlement.

clue.text: Royal family treasuring good times over in European city

indicators.note: treasuring means holding something dear, so the family name holds the other letters

parts.note: the Stuarts were a royal house of Scotland and England

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the letters for good times are reversed

parts.note: T is an abbreviation for time; in maths a times sign, so two give TT

explanation.surface: A royal family looks back fondly on good times in a European city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good times over' reads as nostalgia, but 'over' tells you to reverse the letters. The Stuarts ruled Scotland, and later England too, in the 1600s.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuttgart is a large German city, the capital of Baden-Wurttemberg.

clue.text: See 23
Criminal director invented language books changed into Dutch

indicators.note: changed into means the books letters are swapped for the letter for Dutch

parts.note: Esperanto is an artificial language created in the 1880s
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A film director has his Esperanto books translated into Dutch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'books' is a crossword staple for the New Testament, not a director's library; those two letters give way to the abbreviation for Dutch.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless outlaw, a lawbreaker of the Wild West kind.

clue.text: Very funny! Motown's Diana cuddled by ladies perhaps, then leaves

parts.note: LOL, laughing out loud, is the texting response to something very funny

indicators.note: someone cuddled by others is held within their arms, so the singer goes inside

parts.note: the ladies is a women's toilet, an example of a loo
Diana Ross, Motown star of the Supremes

explanation.surface: A comic scene: Diana Ross is hugged by some women and then walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: LOL + LO(ROSS)O. 'Leaves' looks like a verb, someone departing, but it is the noun: salad leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Lollo rosso is a frilly red-tinged Italian lettuce sold for its salad leaves.

clue.text: So poorly articulated

indicators.note: articulated means spoken out, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: poorly means unwell

explanation.surface: Someone speaking in a sloppy, slurred way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poorly' looks like an adverb on 'articulated', but it is the British word for ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Sic is Latin for thus or so, used in brackets to show a quoted error is reproduced as found.

clue.text: Blow away

parts.note: surface reading: to amaze or overwhelm an audience; setter's reading: a gale carrying something off, seizing it by force of weather

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means to impress hugely, but the setter also pictures a wind literally making off with something.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a place by storm is to captivate it completely, exactly as blowing an audience away means.
